subject: Next steps & affordability: inference pilot options for Payyard
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@payyard.com>, Priya Menon <priya@payyard.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & affordability: inference pilot options for Payyard

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. I focused this on inference economics and the concrete levers we discussed so you can take this to finance.

Pain points you described
- High latency and cost on nightly reconciliation and fraud scoring (peak QPS ~1600, sustained 400-600 QPS).
- Current vendor costs are spiking with new features; you need predictable per-month spend.
- Regulatory requirement to isolate cardholder data processing and maintain audit logs.

Goals we heard
- Reduce per-API call inference cost by 40% vs current vendor within 3 months.
- Achieve <150ms p95 for online scoring for low-latency flows.
- Pilot within an isolated environment (VPC or dedicated tenancy) to satisfy compliance.

Economics & levers (rough, call-level estimates)
- Baseline: your reported traffic maps to ~1.2B tokens/month (combined requests).
- Levers that move the needle: batching (concurrent request aggregation) + prefix/KV caching for common templates + model quantization.
- Quick TCO delta: Hosted baseline (no batching) estimate ~$95k/mo. With conservative batching + cache we project $58k–$68k/mo. Heavy batching + quantization (pilot config) could hit ~$42k/mo. See attached pilot_estimate_v1.xlsx for the scenarios.

Constraints & risks
- If the pilot cannot use caching (due to privacy constraints or request variety) the savings compress substantially.
- Dedicated capacity adds a fixed monthly commitment which helps predictability but needs procurement sign-off.

Proposed next steps
1) Short 60-min technical & finance workshop (Ben + Michael from our side) — we’ll walk the spreadsheet, validate your traffic shape, and align on measurable success criteria.
2) Provide SOC2 scope and evidence checklist for your security team (attached SOC2-ask.pdf).
3) If workshop looks good, we’ll spin a 4-week pilot: sandbox keys, sample model profile, and a committed throughput bucket for predictable pricing.

Can you confirm: 1) an internal budget band (approx $40k–$80k/mo acceptable?) and 2) 3 possible times next week for the workshop? I’ve proposed some times here: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/5d6f7a-workshop-propose

Thanks —

Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: pilot_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, cost scenarios); SOC2-ask.pdf (security checklist)
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@payyard.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@payyard.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & affordability: inference pilot options for Payyard

Michael —

Appreciate the clear note and the file. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync:  
- Traffic: peak numbers are correct, but sustained QPS often spikes during batch windows — estimate closer to 800–1,000 sustained during nightly runs.
- Compliance: Priya (cc) will need to confirm whether caching prefixes in our environment is permitted; if not, the cache savings won’t be available.
- Budget: leadership gave a hard constraint for Q3 pilots — we can go up to ~$50k/month committed for an initial pilot, but anything above requires VP approval.

If the project requires a >$60k/month commitment even with batching, it will be tough. Can you show a scenario that keeps us at or under $50k/mo with realistic assumptions (i.e., limited cache)? Also need a high-level note on the punchlist for SOC2/PCI overlap.

Priya — assigning to you for the caching/compliance question.

—Samir

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@payyard.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@payyard.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & affordability: inference pilot options for Payyard

Samir —

Thanks for the quick note and the budget guardrail. I’ve revisited the estimate with more conservative assumptions (no prefix cache initially, modest batching only). Highlights below — I'll attach an updated spreadsheet in the workshop invite.

Conservative scenario (no prefix cache, modest batching ~1.6x effective throughput)
- Expected token volume mapped to runtime: ~1.2B tokens/month.
- Per-token hosted cost (conservative model) -> $0.000048/token => raw compute ~$58k/mo.
- Apply our volume discounts + batching SLA credit -> projected ~$49k/mo (hosted, limited caching).

Dedicated small-pool option (predictability with a monthly commit)
- Fixed commitment: ~$35k/mo + variable usage ~10k–15k/mo => total ~$45k–$50k/mo (better predictability and auditability).

Interpretation: With the constraints you mentioned, we can craft a pilot at or below the $50k/mo cap by using modest batching and a small dedicated pool — this reduces surprise variable spend while meeting compliance constraints.

Recommended short next steps from our side
- 60-min workshop with your infra/security and our SE (Ben) to validate the lack-of-cache scenario and confirm traffic shape (I suggest Mon/Tue next week).
- Ben will prepare a stripped-down pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx that keeps cache=0 assumptions and lays out the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
- We’ll prepare a one-pager on SOC2 vs PCI overlap that Priya can share (quick note on required logs, KMS usage, and audit window).

I’ll drop proposed slots in the calendar and Ben will attach the updated spreadsheet. If that maps, we can sign a short 4-week pilot commitment that fits your $50k/month constraint.

Cheers —

Michael

Subject: Fwd: Next steps & affordability: inference pilot options for Payyard

Samir / Priya — forwarding the confirmed plan and attaching pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx which models the no-cache conservative scenario + a small dedicated pool line. I’ll host the workshop and walk through the spreadsheet.

Quick summary of agreed next actions:  
1) 60-min workshop (SE-led) — validate traffic and confirm caching constraints; Michael to align schedule.
2) We’ll deliver pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx (attached) + one-pager on SOC2/PCI overlap before the workshop.
3) If Payyard signs the 4-week pilot, we’ll provision a small dedicated pool and sandbox keys; success defined as 40% cost reduction vs current vendor on equivalent traffic shape.

Proposed workshop slots (all PT)
- Mon 26 May, 10:00–11:00
- Tue 27 May, 14:00–15:00
- Wed 28 May, 09:00–10:00

Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0129
